title: Real Madrid 5-1 PSV: Bellingham brilliance headlines rampant Champions League comeback
subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutReal Madrid 5-1 PSV: Bellingham brilliance headlines rampant Champions League comebackShareReal Madrid found themselves a goal behind once again in the Champions League, but they turned on the style in the second half to beat PSV.Real Madrid maintained their 100% record in the Champions League as they came from a goal behind to thrash PSV 5-1 at the Estadio Bernabeu.
Ivan Perisic's 32nd-minute penalty had given PSV a deserved lead, with Jose Mourinho responding by making three half-time changes.
And Madrid duly flipped the script, with Federico Valverde's equaliser early in the second half followed up by substitute Jude Bellingham's stunning 60th-minute volley.
Kylian Mbappe netted twice to continue his scoring run in the Champions League, with Vinicius Junior sealing the win three minutes from time for Los Blancos.
PSV duo Sven Mijnans and Ruben van Bommel both spurned glorious chances to test Thibaut Courtois in the first five minutes.
Sergino Dest's deflected effort then rippled the side netting, with Madrid's first foray forward resulting in Vinicius' rasping 11th-minute curler rattling Matej Kovar's crossbar.

But the visitors' pressure was rewarded midway through the first half. Aurelien Tchouameni was penalised for a foul on Mijnans, with the foul given after a VAR review. PSV captain Perisic stepped up and coolly dispatched the spot-kick.
Madrid were jeered off at half-time, but Mourinho's triple change sparked them into life, with Valverde getting the comeback started with a fine finish after Arda Guler's neat flick.

The turnaround was complete following a moment of individual brilliance from Bellingham, who flicked a loose ball up a couple of times before sending a sensational strike in off the right post on the hour.

Kodai Sano was then ruthlessly punished after trying to play out from the back, with his sloppy pass allowing Guler to tee up Mbappe in the 64th minute, with the Frenchman grabbing his second six minutes from time when he rounded Kovar to score.
But there was still time for Vinicius to add more gloss, with Bellingham's searching ball sending him clear before he poked through the legs of the PSV goalkeeper.
Mbappe scores again for Mourinho's comeback kings

Despite coming into the game with 12 points from their first four games, Madrid's Champions League campaign had been anything but straightforward, needing to come from behind to earn dramatic wins against Roma and AEK Athens.

And they were forced to do things the hard way once again when Perisic tucked away his penalty. At 37 years and 295 days old, he became the oldest goalscorer against Madrid in the Champions League, leaving Mourinho with plenty to ponder at the break.

He chose to withdraw Antonio Rudiger, Eder Militao and Tchouameni, and the difference was clear to see. In the last two seasons, Madrid have now won six Champions League matches when conceding first (L2), more than any other side.
And it was the quality already on the pitch that finally showed up. Mbappe attempted nine shots and has now scored in his last seven Champions League appearances for Madrid.

Since 1955, only Cristiano Ronaldo has had a longer run for the club, netting in 11 in a row between June 2017 and April 2018, and eight on the spin between September 2013 and April 2014, while it marks Mbappe's longest scoring run in the competition.
Bellingham, though, stole the show with that sumptuous piece of skill. The England star had three shots, created three chances and won 3/4 duels during his time on the pitch.

Madrid have now started a Champions League campaign with five consecutive wins for the fourth time, but Mourinho will still want to see improvements, despite watching his side rack up an expected goals (xG) value of 4.79 from their 24 shots to PSV's tally of 1.69 from their 10 attempts.
